label: thm:intro-matrix
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-matrix}
Let $K$ be a field, put
$R=K[[x_1,\ldots,x_s]]$, $\mathfrak m=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_s\rangle$, and
$M_{m,n}=\operatorname{Mat}(m,n,R)$.  We write
$\mathcal R=\operatorname{Aut}_K(R)$,
$\mathcal G_l=\operatorname{GL}_m(R)\rtimes\mathcal R$,
$\mathcal G_r=\operatorname{GL}_n(R)^{\mathrm{op}}\rtimes\mathcal R$, and
$\mathcal G_{lr}=(\operatorname{GL}_m(R)\times\operatorname{GL}_n(R)^{\mathrm{op}})\rtimes\mathcal R$.
For $1\le t\le\min(m,n)$, let $I_t(A)$ be the ideal generated by the
$t\times t$ minors of $A$ and put
$c_t=(m-t+1)(n-t+1)$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item For $G\in\{\mathcal R,\mathcal G_{lr}\}$, finite $G$-determinacy is equivalent to
finite codimension of the $G$-tangent image.  If $K$ is infinite, the
same equivalence holds for $G\in\{\mathcal G_l,\mathcal G_r\}$.  Over an arbitrary field,
the one-sided equivalence also holds when $n\le m$ and $s\le m-n+1$ for $\mathcal G_l$, and when $m\le n$ and $ s\le n-m+1$ for $\mathcal G_r$; see Theorems~\ref{thm:glr},
\ref{thm:one-sided-complete}, \ref{thm:one-sided-ranges},
and~\ref{thm:pure-right}.

\item A proper ideal $I\subseteq R$ with $\dim\left(\frac{R}{I}\right)>0$
is finitely contact determined if and only if
$\frac{R}{I}$ is an isolated complete-intersection singularity; see
Corollary~\ref{cor:icis-all-fields}.

\item If $A$ is finitely determined for one of the actions
$\mathcal R,\mathcal G_l,\mathcal G_r,\mathcal G_{lr}$, then, for every
$1\le t\le\min\{m,n\}$ we have $\operatorname{ht} I_t(A)
=
\min\{s,(m-t+1)(n-t+1)\}$;
see Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new}.

\item Under the hypotheses of \textup{(iii)}, the quotient $\frac{R}{I_t(A)}$
is Cohen--Macaulay.  Moreover, it is reduced if $(m-t+1)(n-t+1)<s$, and it is a normal domain if $(m-t+1)(n-t+1)\le s-2$; 
see Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new}.
\end{enumerate}

label: thm:intro-hypersurface
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-hypersurface}
Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic $p>0$, and let $f$ be an isolated
hypersurface germ.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item We have $\operatorname{Fmod}(f)\le\operatorname{pmod}(f)=\operatorname{Rmod}(f)$; see Proposition~\ref{prop:Flower} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:pmod-rmod-general}.
\item We have
$\mu(f)+c(f)\le p^{c(f)}\bigl(\operatorname{Fmod}(f)+1\bigr)$. Consequently, we have that
$\mu(f)\le p^{\,2+\sqrt[3]{6\operatorname{Rmod}(f)}}\bigl(\operatorname{Rmod}(f)+1\bigr)$; see Corollary~\ref{cor:stable-milnor-growth}.

\item For every $D\ge0$, the residual number of variables, Milnor number,
multiplicity, and right-classification radius of all isolated germs with
$\operatorname{Rmod}(f)\le D$ are bounded in terms of $p$ and $D$.  Moreover, there is an integer
$\widehat N_{p,D}$, independent of the original ambient dimension, such that every such
$f$ is right $\widehat N_{p,D}$-determined; see Theorem~\ref{thm:uniform} annd
Corollary~\ref{cor:uniform-full-determinacy}.
\end{enumerate}

label: thm:intro-Fapplications
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:intro-Fapplications}
Fix $p>0$ and $D\ge0$, and let $f$ be isolated with $\operatorname{Rmod}(f)\le D$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item Every $F$-jumping number of $\langle f\rangle$ in $(0,1]$ belongs to a finite set
$\Xi_{p,D}$ depending only on $p,D$; see Theorem~\ref{thm:universal-Fjump-spectrum}.
\item There is an integer $E_{p,D}$ such that the single Frobenius-level invariant
$\nu_{E_{p,D}}(f)$ determines $\operatorname{fpt}(f)$; see Theorem~\ref{thm:one-level-fpt}. 
\item If $\frac{R}{\langle f\rangle}$ is reduced, then the number of $F$-jumping coefficients in
$[0,1]$ and the colength of its finitistic test ideal are bounded in terms of $p,D$.
Moreover, a power of the maximal ideal, with exponent depending only on $p,D$, is
contained in the Jacobian ideal and hence in the finitistic test ideal; see Corollary~\ref{cor:test-uniform}. 
\item Only finitely many eventual sequences of level-$e$ positive-characteristic
Bernstein--Sato root sets occur at fixed $p,D$; Corollary~\ref{cor:finite-BS-sequences}.
\end{enumerate}
In addition, the numerical $F$-jumping spectrum is uniformly $\mathfrak m$-adically constant in
the sense of Corollary~\ref{cor:uniform-m-adic-constancy}.

title: Question

$G\in\{\mathcal R,\mathcal G_l,\mathcal G_r,\mathcal G_{lr}\}$?\\

name: GLS Conjecture 3.1.16

title: Remark
body_md:
Finite determinacy for smooth and analytic map germs goes back to the work of Mather on
finitely determined map germs \cite{Mather1968}.  For hypersurface functions over
fields of arbitrary characteristic, finite right determinacy is equivalent to finiteness
of the Milnor number by Boubakri--Greuel--Markwig \cite{BoubakriGreuelMarkwig2012}.
For matrices in positive characteristic, Greuel--Pham introduced the tangent image in
order to separate the infinitesimal image of the orbit map from the tangent space of a
possibly inseparable orbit \cite{GP18}.  This distinction is the source of Question~A.
For determinacy and Mather--Yau-type phenomena over complete regular local rings in
mixed characteristic, see \cite{SvorayDVR2025}.

label: lem:dense-transfer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dense-transfer}
Let a group $G$ act on an $\mathfrak m$-adically filtered set $E$, and let $P$ be a
$G$-invariant property.  Suppose that for every $A\in E$ and every $N$
there exists $B\in A+\mathfrak m^N E$ satisfying $P$.  Then every finitely
$G$-determined element of $E$ satisfies $P$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $A$ is $k$-$G$-determined, choose $B\in A+\mathfrak m^{k+1}E$ satisfying $P$.
Then $A\sim_G B$, so $P(A)$ follows from $G$-invariance.

label: prop:generic-rank
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:generic-rank}
Let $G\in\{\mathcal R,\mathcal G_l,\mathcal G_r,\mathcal G_{lr}\}$ and let $A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}$ be finitely $G$-determined.  Then $\operatorname{rank}_{\operatorname{Frac}(R)}A=\min(m,n)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $r=\min(m,n)$ and suppose that $A$ is $k$-$G$-determined.  Fix an
$r\times r$ submatrix $A_0$ of $A$, and choose $N\ge k+1$.  For
$\lambda=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)\in K^r$, perturb the diagonal of
that block by
$\lambda_1x_1^N,\ldots,\lambda_rx_1^N$
(with $x_1$ used repeatedly; no distinct variables are needed), leaving
all other entries unchanged.  Call the resulting matrix $B_\lambda$.
Then
$B_\lambda-A\in\mathfrak m^N M_{m,n}$.
The determinant of the chosen block of $B_\lambda$ is a polynomial
$P(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r)\in R[\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_r]$
which has degree at most one in each $\lambda_i$ and whose coefficient of
$\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_r$ is $x_1^{Nr}\ne0$.\\

A nonzero polynomial of degree at most one in each variable cannot vanish
on all of $K^r$: this follows by induction on $r$ from the one-variable
fact, valid over every field.  Hence for some $\lambda\in K^r$ the chosen
$r\times r$ minor of $B_\lambda$ is nonzero.  Therefore
$\operatorname{rank}_{\operatorname{Frac}(R)}B_\lambda=r$. Finite determinacy gives $B_\lambda\sim_G A$.  Generic rank is invariant
under source automorphisms and under invertible row and column operations.
Therefore $A$ also has generic rank $r$.
head: environment

label: prop:dimension-bounds
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $A$ is $k$-determined and fix $\ell>k$.  The set of $\ell$-jets
having the same $k$-jet as $A$ is an affine cylinder of dimension
$mn(D_\ell-D_k)$.
For an infinite field, all its $K$-points lie in the $\ell$-jet orbit of
$A$, hence the Zariski closure of that orbit has dimension at least this
number. The $\ell$-jet automorphism group is the open subset of $\mathfrak m R_\ell^s$
on which the linear part is invertible.  Hence its dimension is exactly
$s(D_\ell-1)$.  Likewise, $\operatorname{GL}_m(R_\ell)$ and $\operatorname{GL}_n(R_\ell)$ are open
subsets of $M_m(R_\ell)$ and $M_n(R_\ell)$, so their dimensions are exactly
$m^2D_\ell$ and $n^2D_\ell$.  Since orbit dimension is at most group
dimension, division by $D_\ell$ followed by $\ell\to\infty$ gives the
asserted inequalities.\\

If $K=\mathbb F_q$, we use cardinalities instead.  The cylinder contains
$q^{mn(D_\ell-D_k)}$ points.  Reduction modulo $\mathfrak m$ gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 |\operatorname{Aut}_K(R_\ell)|&=|\operatorname{GL}_s(\mathbb F_q)|q^{s(D_\ell-1-s)},\\
 |\operatorname{GL}_m(R_\ell)|&=|\operatorname{GL}_m(\mathbb F_q)|q^{m^2(D_\ell-1)},\\
 |\operatorname{GL}_n(R_\ell)|&=|\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)|q^{n^2(D_\ell-1)}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The orbit has cardinality at most that of the acting jet group.  Taking $\log_q$,
dividing by $D_\ell$, and passing to the limit gives the same bounds.

label: lem:poonen
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poonen}
Let $K=\mathbb F_q$.  Fix a quasiprojective embedding of a $K$-scheme $X$ into
projective space, let $Z$ be a finite subscheme of the ambient projective space, and suppose $U=X-(X\cap Z)$ is smooth of pure dimension $d>0$.  Given arbitrary prescribed Taylor
data on $Z$, there exists, in sufficiently large degree, a hypersurface
having exactly those Taylor data and whose intersection with $U$ is smooth
of pure dimension $d-1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the Bertini theorem of Poonen with Taylor conditions
\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Poonen}.  If $T$ is the singleton consisting of the
prescribed restriction on $Z$, the density appearing in the theorem of Poonen
is positive.  Importantly, $X$ need not be smooth along $Z$; only
$U=X-(X\cap Z)$ is required to be smooth.
head: environment

label: lem:poonen-local
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poonen-local}
Let $K=\mathbb F_q$, let $Z$ be a finite subscheme of a projective space, and let $X_1,\ldots,X_u$ be smooth quasiprojective subschemes. Fix Taylor data on $Z$. Then, in sufficiently large degree, there exists a hypersurface realizing those Taylor data such that, away from $Z$, its intersection with every positive-dimensional $X_i$ is smooth of the expected dimension and it avoids every zero-dimensional $X_i$.
head: environment
name: Local-conditions principle over finite fields

title: Proof
body_md: Apply \cite[Theorem~1.3]{Poonen}. At a closed point $P\notin Z$, simultaneous smoothness is a condition on the value and first derivatives of the hypersurface section. For each $X_i$ containing $P$, the bad first jets are those for which the value and all tangent derivatives along $X_i$ vanish. These are precisely the local smoothness conditions occurring in Poonen's closed-point sieve. The prescribed Taylor class changes only the finitely many local conditions supported on $Z$. Poonen's convergence estimates for the sieve therefore give a positive limiting density, and hence such hypersurfaces exist in sufficiently large degree.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Classical Bertini arguments over infinite fields obtain smooth members by removing a
proper closed subset of a linear system.  Over a finite field such an open set need not
have a rational point.  Poonen replaced this genericity argument by a closed-point sieve
and proved positive-density Bertini theorems, including prescribed Taylor conditions
\cite{Poonen}.  Recent work of Bertucci develops further forms of Taylor conditions over
finite fields \cite{Bertucci}; Ajit--Bertucci prove complementary finite-field Bertini
theorems preserving Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity \cite{AjitBertucci2026}.
head: environment

label: prop:icis-density
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:icis-density}
Let $K=\mathbb F_q$ and let $r<s$.  For arbitrary
$h_1,\ldots,h_r\in\mathfrak m$ and every $N\ge1$, there exist $g_1,\ldots,g_r\in\mathfrak m$ such that $g_i\equiv h_i\pmod{\mathfrak m^N}$ and $\frac{R}{\langle g_1,\ldots,g_r\rangle}$ is an isolated complete-intersection
singularity.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The successive construction in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:icis}
uses no finite-determinacy assumption until its final transport step.
Applying Lemma~\ref{lem:poonen} successively produces a complete
intersection that is smooth off the origin and realizes the prescribed
jet.  The height and Jacobian arguments given below then show that its
completion is an ICIS.
head: environment

label: thm:icis
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:icis}
Let $K=\mathbb F_q$, let $R=K[[x_1,\ldots,x_s]]$, and let $I$ be a proper
ideal with $\dim \left(\frac{R}{I}\right)>0$.  If $I$ is finitely contact determined, then
$\frac{R}{I}$ is an isolated complete-intersection singularity.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose a minimal system $I=\langle h_1,\ldots,h_r\rangle$.  We first show that $r<s$.
The field-independent part of \cite[Theorem~3.1.22(2)]{GLS}, equivalently
\cite[Theorem~2.6]{GP19}, implies that if a finitely determined
$r\times1$ column has $r\ge s$, then the ideal generated by its entries
contains a power of $\mathfrak m$.  This would make $\frac{R}{I}$ zero-dimensional.  Hence
$r<s$.\\

Choose a determinacy order $k$, and choose $N\ge k+1$.  Let
$Z=\operatorname{Spec}\!\left(\frac{P}{\mathfrak m_0^N}\right)$.
For each $i$, let $h_i^{<N}\in\mathfrak m_0$ be the polynomial truncation of $h_i$
modulo $\mathfrak m^N$.  Its class in $\frac{P}{\mathfrak m_0^N}=H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ is the Taylor
data to be prescribed.\\

We construct polynomials $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ successively, each satisfying
$g_i\equiv h_i^{<N}\pmod{\mathfrak m_0^N}$, equivalently $g_i-h_i\in\mathfrak m^NR$ after
completion.  Put $X_0=\mathbb A_K^s$, and after choosing the
first $i$ equations put
$X_i=V(g_1,\ldots,g_i)$.
We require $X_i-\{0\}$ to be smooth of pure dimension $s-i$.\\

The assertion holds for $X_0$.  Assuming it for $X_{i-1}$, apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:poonen} to $X_{i-1}$, with the fixed fat point $Z$ and the
prescribed Taylor class of $h_i^{<N}$.  Since $Z$ is supported at the origin,
the smooth open set in \cite[Theorem~1.2]{Poonen} is precisely
$X_{i-1}-\{0\}$.  We obtain $g_i$ such that $X_i-\{0\}$ is smooth of pure
dimension $s-i$.  Induction gives $X_r-\{0\}$ smooth of dimension
$s-r>0$.\\

Let $J=\langle g_1,\ldots,g_r\rangle S_0$.  Since $J$ has $r$
generators, every minimal prime has height at most $r$.  A minimal prime
cannot be $\mathfrak m_0$, because $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak m_0=s>r$.  Therefore each irreducible
component meets the punctured spectrum.  On the punctured spectrum $\frac{S_0}{J}$
is smooth of pure dimension $s-r$, hence each minimal prime has height
exactly $r$.  Thus $J$ has height $r$.  Since $S_0$ is regular, hence Cohen--Macaulay, and $J$ has height $r$, the $r$ generators form a regular sequence \cite[Lemmas~10.106.3 and~10.104.2, Tags~00NQ and~02JN]{stacks-project}.\\

Because a finite field is perfect, the Jacobian criterion applies \cite[Lemma~10.137.15, Tag~00TE]{stacks-project}.  Let
$\operatorname{JacMat}(g)$ be the $r\times s$ Jacobian matrix.  Smoothness of
$X_r-\{0\}$ implies that
$J+I_r(\operatorname{JacMat}(g))$
is either the unit ideal or has radical $\mathfrak m_0$.  Hence it contains a power
of $\mathfrak m_0$.  Since completion is faithfully flat, it preserves the regular sequence
\cite[Lemma~10.68.5, Tag~00LM]{stacks-project}; the maximal-ideal-primary Jacobian
condition is preserved as well.  Consequently
$\frac{R}{\langle g_1,\ldots,g_r\rangle}$ is an ICIS in the sense of
\cite[Definition 3.1.27 and Theorem 3.1.28]{GLS}.\\

By construction, every $g_i-h_i$ lies in
$\mathfrak m^N\subseteq\mathfrak m^{k+1}$.  Finite contact $k$-determinacy therefore gives
an isomorphism of complete local $K$-algebras
$\frac{R}{I}\cong \frac{R}{\langle g_1,\ldots,g_r\rangle}$.
The complete-intersection property and regularity away from the closed
point are intrinsic properties of this local algebra.  Hence $\frac{R}{I}$ is an
ICIS.

label: lem:rank
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:rank}
For $C\in\Sigma_r$, one has $T_C\Sigma_r=M_m(K)C+C M_n(K)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The rank-$r$ stratum is the
$\operatorname{GL}_m(K)\times\operatorname{GL}_n(K)$-orbit of $C$.  Differentiating the orbit map gives
$M_m(K)C+C M_n(K)\subseteq T_C\Sigma_r$.
Putting $C$ into normal form with an $r\times r$ identity block shows that
the left-hand side consists precisely of matrices whose lower-right
$(m-r)\times(n-r)$ block vanishes.  Its dimension is $r(m+n-r)$, which is
the dimension of $\Sigma_r$.  Therefore equality holds in every characteristic.

label: thm:stratified-jet
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write the coordinates of $V$ as $y_1,\ldots,y_d$, put
$E=\mathbb A_K^s\times V$, and let $z=(0,0)$.  Write
$A=(A_1,\ldots,A_d)$, and let $A_\beta^{<N}$ be the polynomial truncation of
$A_\beta$ modulo $\mathfrak m^N$.\\

We construct polynomial equations $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ recursively so that
$h_\beta$ has the prescribed $(N-1)$-jet
$y_\beta-A_\beta^{<N}(x)$
at $z$.  Put $\Gamma_i=V(h_1,\ldots,h_i)$.  The inductive requirement is
that, away from $z$, $\Gamma_i$ and every nonempty
$\Gamma_i\cap(\mathbb A_K^s\times S_\alpha)$
are smooth of the expected dimensions. Assume $h_1,\ldots,h_{i-1}$ have been chosen.  We regard the relevant affine
schemes as quasiprojective subschemes of one projective space and homogenize the
polynomials.  This allows us to use one ambient linear system throughout; no condition is
imposed at infinity.\\

Suppose first that $K$ is finite.  By the inductive hypothesis, the quasiprojective
schemes
\[
 X_0=\Gamma_{i-1}\setminus\{z\},\qquad
 X_\alpha=\bigl(\Gamma_{i-1}\cap(\mathbb A_K^s\times S_\alpha)\bigr)\setminus\{z\}
\]
are smooth whenever nonempty; zero-dimensional members are allowed.  We use these finitely
many schemes as the $X_j$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:poonen-local}.  At $z$ we prescribe the unique
coset modulo the $N$-th power of the maximal ideal giving the required $(N-1)$-jet.  This
coset is open and closed in the completed local ring and hence has positive Haar measure and
boundary of measure zero.\\

Now let $P\ne z$ be a closed point.  For every positive-dimensional $X_j$ containing $P$ we
allow precisely those first jets for which either $h_i(P)\ne0$, or $h_i(P)=0$ and
\[
 dh_i(P)|_{T_PX_j}\ne0.
\]
This is exactly the condition that the hypersurface section of $X_j$ be smooth of dimension
$\dim X_j-1$ at $P$.  If $X_j$ is zero-dimensional, the expected dimension is $-1$, and we
require $h_i(P)\ne0$.  At points lying on none of the $X_j$ there is no condition.  For each fixed $X_j$ containing $P$, the bad first jets form a proper linear subspace of the value-and-first-derivative space. Imposing the condition simultaneously for all $X_j$ through $P$ removes a finite union of such proper linear subspaces. In particular, the allowed set is a finite-jet cylinder of positive local measure—every jet with $h_i(P)\ne0$ is allowed—and its boundary has measure zero.  At a point of a stratum $S_\alpha$, the tangent space of $\Gamma_{i-1}\cap(\mathbb A_K^s\times S_\alpha)$ is contained in $T_P\Gamma_{i-1}$. Hence, whenever both conditions occur, the imposed condition on the stratified intersection is compatible with the ambient smoothness condition.\\

All hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:poonen-local} are therefore satisfied, and an admissible
$h_i$ exists.  This is the same closed-point-sieve mechanism used in
\cite[Theorem~3.3]{Poonen}, now with the finite Taylor condition at $z$ kept independent of
the punctured smoothness conditions.\\

Now suppose that $K$ is infinite.  Let $L_D$ be the affine space of polynomials of degree
at most $D$ with the prescribed jet at $z$.  For $D\gg0$, its translation space separates
first jets at every geometric point of $E\setminus\{z\}$.  Indeed, at a point
$P\ne z$ one may choose a linear form vanishing at $z$ and nonvanishing at $P$, raise it
to the $N$-th power, and multiply by affine linear functions to obtain arbitrary value and
tangent data at $P$.  Let $X$ be one of the finitely many smooth schemes occurring in the
induction and put $e=\dim X$.  For fixed $P\in X$, failure of a hypersurface section to
have the expected smoothness is given by the $e+1$ independent linear conditions $h_i(P)=0$ and $dh_i(P)|_{T_PX}=0$ when $e>0$, and by the single condition $h_i(P)=0$ when $e=0$.  Hence the corresponding incidence variety in $L_D\times X$ has dimension at most $\dim L_D-1$. The Zariski closure of its projection in $L_D$ therefore has dimension at most $\dim L_D-1$, and is a proper closed subset.  Removing the finitely many bad
projections leaves a nonempty Zariski-open subset of $L_D$, and an infinite field has a
$K$-rational point in this open set.  Choosing that point completes the induction.\\

After $d$ steps put $\Gamma=\Gamma_d$.  At $z$ we have
$\left(\frac{\partial h_\alpha}{\partial y_\beta}\right)(z)=I_d$,
so the projection $\Gamma\to\mathbb A_K^s$ is étale at $z$.  The formal
implicit-function theorem identifies the completed germ of $\Gamma$ at
$z$ with the graph of a unique formal map $B(x)$, and the prescribed jets
give $B-A\in\mathfrak m^N R^d$.  After shrinking to an étale neighborhood
$W$ of the distinguished point, the $y$-coordinate map $F:W\to V$ is
transverse to every $S_\alpha$ away from that point.

label: thm:jettrans
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:jettrans}
Let $K$ be an arbitrary field, let
$A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}(K[[x_1,\ldots,x_s]])$, and let $N\ge2$.  There exists $B$
with the same $(N-1)$-jet as $A$ such that the extended $\mathcal G_{lr}$-tangent
image of $B$ has finite $K$-codimension.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified-jet} to the finite rank stratification
$Y=\coprod_r\Sigma_r$.  At every point away from the origin, transversality and
Lemma~\ref{lem:rank} therefore give that
$dB(T)+M_m B+B M_n=M_{m,n}$.
Equivalently, the coherent homomorphism
\[
M_m(\mathcal O_W)\oplus M_n(\mathcal O_W)\oplus T_W
\longrightarrow M_{m,n}(\mathcal O_W),
\qquad
(U,V,\xi)\longmapsto UB+BV+dB(\xi),
\]
is surjective away from the distinguished point.  Its cokernel is
therefore supported at that point and has finite length.  Completion
identifies its image with the extended tangent image of the formal germ
$B$.
head: environment

label: cor:glr-dense
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:glr-dense}
For every $A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}$ and every
$N$ there exists $B\equiv A\pmod{\mathfrak m^N}$ that is finitely
$\mathcal G_{lr}$-determined.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:jettrans} gives $B$ with finite tangent-image codimension.
The arbitrary-field sufficient criterion
\cite[Theorem~3.1.12]{GLS} then gives finite determinacy.
head: environment

label: thm:glr
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:glr}
For every field $K$ and every
$A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}(K[[x_1,\ldots,x_s]])$, finite $\mathcal G_{lr}$-determinacy implies
finite codimension of the tangent image.  Together with the sufficient
criterion of Greuel--Pham, this gives the equivalence predicted by
Conjecture~3.1.16 for the full left--right group.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose $A$ is $k$-$\mathcal G_{lr}$-determined, and choose $N\ge k+1$.  By
Theorem~\ref{thm:jettrans}, choose $B$ with
$B-A\in\mathfrak m^N M_{m,n}$ and with tangent image of finite codimension.  Finite
determinacy gives $A\sim_{\mathcal G_{lr}}B$. Finite codimension of the tangent image is invariant under
$\mathcal G_{lr}$-equivalence, by the chain rule and invertibility of the row,
column, and coordinate transformations.  Hence the tangent image of $A$
has finite codimension.  The converse is the arbitrary-characteristic
sufficient criterion \cite[Theorem 3.1.12]{GLS}.
head: environment

label: def:infinitesimal-orbit-stratification
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:infinitesimal-orbit-stratification}
A finite smooth stratification
$V=\coprod_{\alpha=1}^t S_\alpha$
is called an \emph{infinitesimal-orbit stratification} if, after every
field extension, at every point $v\in S_\alpha$ we have that
$\mathfrak h\cdot v=T_vS_\alpha$.
head: environment

label: thm:abstract-current
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:abstract-current}
Assume that $V$ admits a finite infinitesimal-orbit stratification.  Then,
by Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified-jet}, every finitely
$\mathcal G_H$-determined formal map $A$ satisfies
\[
\dim_K \left(\frac{V\otimes_KR}{\widetilde T_A^{\,e}}\right)<\infty.
\]
Whenever finite codimension of this infinitesimal module is known to be
sufficient for finite determinacy for the action under consideration, it
is therefore equivalent to finite determinacy.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Theorem~\ref{thm:stratified-jet} shows that every $\mathfrak m$-adic cylinder around
$A$ contains a germ $B$ transverse away from the origin to all strata.
At a point with $B(x)\in S_\alpha$, we have that
$dB_x(T_x)+T_{B(x)}S_\alpha=T_{B(x)}V$.
By the infinitesimal-orbit hypothesis, we therefore get that
$dB_x(T_x)+\mathfrak h\cdot B(x)=T_{B(x)}V$.
Therefore the coherent cokernel of the infinitesimal current-orbit map is
supported only at the origin, so its completion has finite length.
Finite codimension of the infinitesimal module is invariant under the
current action.  Lemma~\ref{lem:dense-transfer} now transports the property
from $B$ to every finitely determined $A$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
For $V=M_{m,n}$ and $H=\operatorname{GL}_m\times\operatorname{GL}_n$, the rank strata form an
infinitesimal-orbit stratification by Lemma~\ref{lem:rank}.  Thus
Theorem~\ref{thm:glr} is the basic matrix instance of
Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract-current}.
head: environment

label: lem:grass-quotient
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:grass-quotient}
At $C\in\Sigma_r$, the kernel of $d\kappa_r$ is $M_mC$ and the kernel of
$d\iota_r$ is $CM_n$.  Hence the quotient of $T_C\Sigma_r$ by the left matrix orbit
is $T_{\kappa_r(C)}\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)$, while the corresponding quotient by the right
matrix orbit is $T_{\iota_r(C)}\operatorname{Gr}(r,m)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The fibers of $\kappa_r$ are the $\operatorname{GL}_m$-orbits inside $\Sigma_r$, while the fibers
of $\iota_r$ are the $\operatorname{GL}_n$-orbits.  Both maps are smooth homogeneous fibrations.
Differentiating gives the statement.
head: environment

label: prop:one-sided-criterion
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:one-sided-criterion}
Assume that $A$ is transverse to all rank strata on the punctured spectrum.  Then the
extended $\mathcal G_l$ tangent image has finite codimension exactly when every induced kernel
map $\kappa_r\circ A$ is submersive on $A^{-1}(\Sigma_r)$ away from the origin.
Dually, the extended $\mathcal G_r$ tangent image has finite codimension exactly when all
induced image maps $\iota_r\circ A$ are submersive there.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Rank transversality supplies all normal directions to $\Sigma_r$.  By
Lemma~\ref{lem:grass-quotient}, the directions missing from the left matrix orbit are
exactly the tangent directions of the kernel Grassmannian, and they are supplied by the
differential of $\kappa_r\circ A$.  Thus localized surjectivity of the extended left
tangent image is exactly submersivity of the kernel map.  The right case is dual.
Finite codimension is equivalent to localized surjectivity at every nonmaximal prime.
head: environment

label: cor:one-sided-reduction
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:one-sided-reduction}
If $A$ is finitely $\mathcal G_l$-determined, then the only possible obstruction at this stage to finite
codimension of its tangent image is a punctured critical locus of the kernel maps.
Dually, for a finitely $\mathcal G_r$-determined matrix the only possible obstruction at this stage is a
punctured critical locus of the image maps.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: prop:one-sided-full-rank
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:one-sided-full-rank}
If $n\le m$ and $I_n(A)$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary, then $A$ is finitely
$\mathcal G_l$-determined and its extended $\mathcal G_l$ tangent image has finite codimension.
Dually, if $m\le n$ and $I_m(A)$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary, then $A$ is finitely
$\mathcal G_r$-determined.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At a punctured point, full column rank means that $C:K^n\to K^m$ is injective.  Every
$B:K^n\to K^m$ can then be written $B=UC$ for some $U\in M_m(K)$, so the left
matrix directions already fill the target.  Therefore the tangent cokernel has finite length,
and the sufficient tangent-image criterion \cite[Theorem~3.1.12]{GLS} gives finite
determinacy.  The right
case is the transpose.
head: environment

label: thm:one-sided-ranges
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:one-sided-ranges}
If $n\le m$ and $s\le m-n+1$, then finite $\mathcal G_l$-determinacy, $\mathfrak m$-primaryness of
$I_n(A)$, and finite codimension of the extended $\mathcal G_l$ tangent image are equivalent.
Dually, if $m\le n$ and $s\le n-m+1$, the analogous three conditions for $\mathcal G_r$ and
$I_m(A)$ are equivalent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Only necessity of the determinantal condition remains.  Finite one-sided determinacy
implies finite $\mathcal G_{lr}$-determinacy.  Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new} gives
$\operatorname{ht} I_n(A)=\min\{s,m-n+1\}=s$ in the left case, hence $I_n(A)$ is
$\mathfrak m$-primary.  The right case is dual.  The remaining implications are
Proposition~\ref{prop:one-sided-full-rank} and the sufficient criterion
\cite[Theorem~3.1.12]{GLS}.
head: environment

label: lem:deep-gauge-rigidity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}$, the condition $V-I_n\in\mathfrak m^kM_n(R)$ gives
$AV-A\in\mathfrak m^{k+1}M_{m,n}$.  Finite $\mathcal G_l$-determinacy therefore gives
$AV=U\varphi(A)$ for some $U\in\operatorname{GL}_m(R)$ and $\varphi\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(R)$.  Right
multiplication by $V$ and left multiplication by $U$ do not change matrix rank, and
$I_t(AV)=I_t(A)$ while $I_t(U\varphi(A))=\varphi(I_t(A))$.  Hence $\varphi$ preserves
every determinantal rank locus.  On the rank-$r$ locus, left multiplication does not
change the kernel and right multiplication sends the kernel by $V^{-1}$.  Thus the two
kernel maps differ only by the source automorphism induced by $\varphi$.  The proof for
$\mathcal G_r$ is obtained by transposing the argument: left gauges act on image subspaces,
whereas right multiplication does not change them.
head: environment

label: lem:frobenius-gauge-flexibility
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:frobenius-gauge-flexibility}
Assume that $\operatorname{char} K=p>0$ and let $N\ge1$.  Let
$\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$ be a prime of $R$, and put $L=\operatorname{Frac}\left(\frac{R}{\mathfrak q}\right)$.  Then the values at $\mathfrak q$ of $N$-deep polynomial local gauges
$V\in\operatorname{GL}_n(S_0)$ satisfying $dV=0$ are Zariski dense in $\operatorname{GL}_n(L)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Put $\eta=\mathfrak q\cap S_0$. 
Since $\mathfrak q\ne\mathfrak m$, we have that $\eta\ne\mathfrak m_0$.  Therefore we may choose $a\in\mathfrak m_0^N\setminus\eta$.
For $B=[b_{ij}]\in M_n(S_0)$, write $B^{[p]}=(b_{ij}^p)$.
and set $V_B=I_n+a^pB^{[p]}$. 
Since $a\in\mathfrak m_0$, we get that $\det(V_B)\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m_0}$, so $V_B\in\operatorname{GL}_n(S_0)$.  Moreover,
\[
V_B-I_n\in\mathfrak m_0^{Np}M_n(S_0)\subseteq\mathfrak m_0^NM_n(S_0),
\]
and, since all entries added to the identity are $p$-th powers, we have that $dV_B=0$.  The domain $S_0/\eta$ is infinite.  Indeed, this is immediate when $K$ is
infinite, while when $K$ is finite it follows from
$\eta\ne\mathfrak m_0$, because then $S_0/\eta$ has positive dimension.  Frobenius is
injective on this domain, and therefore its set of $p$-th powers is infinite.
Consequently its image in $L$ is Zariski dense in $\mathbb A_L^1$. It follows entrywise that the values $I_n+\overline a^{\,p}B(\mathfrak q)^{[p]}$ are Zariski dense in $M_n(L)$.  Intersecting with the nonempty open subset
$\operatorname{GL}_n(L)$ therefore proves the assertion.
head: environment

label: lem:deep-gauge-general-position
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:deep-gauge-general-position}
Let $K$ be infinite, let $U\subseteq\mathbb A_K^s$ be an
open neighborhood of the origin, and let
$X\subseteq U\setminus\{0\}$ be a smooth locally closed
$K$-subscheme of pure dimension $d$.
Let $F:X\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}(a,n)$ where $t=a(n-a)$ and assume $1\le t\le d$. For every $N\ge1$, there exists a polynomial matrix $V=I_n+H$ with $H\in M_n\bigl(\langle x_1,\ldots,x_s\rangle^N K[x_1,\ldots,x_s]\bigr)$ 
such that on $X_V=X\cap D(\det V)$ we have that $\dim\operatorname{Crit}(V^{-1}\!\cdot F)\le t-1$.  In particular, $V$ defines an $N$-deep element of
$\operatorname{GL}_n(S_0)$. If $t=0$, the critical locus is empty.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $D\ge N+1$, and let $ E_D=\langle x_1,\ldots,x_s\rangle^N \cap K[x_1,\ldots,x_s]_{\le D}$ and $\mathcal{P}_D=M_n(E_D)$. For every geometric point $x\ne0$, evaluation of first jets
gives a surjection $E_D\otimes_K\kappa(x)
   \longrightarrow
   \mathcal O_{\mathbb A^s_{\kappa(x)},x}/\mathfrak m_x^2$. Indeed, choose $x_\nu(x)\ne0$. Multiplication by $x_\nu^N$
is invertible on the first-jet algebra, and affine-linear
polynomials supply all first jets.\\

Consider the open subset $\Omega= \{(x,H)\in X\times\mathcal P_D \colon \det(I_n+H(x))\ne0\}$.
On $\Omega$, the expression $(I_n+H)^{-1}\!\cdot F$ is
defined. Fix a geometric point $x$ and an invertible value
$C=I_n+H(x)$. Keeping this value fixed, the first derivatives
of $H$ can vary arbitrarily. Since the orbit map $\operatorname{GL}_n\longrightarrow\operatorname{Gr}(a,n)$ is smooth, these variations induce arbitrary variations of
the differential in $\operatorname{Hom}_{\kappa(x)} \bigl(T_xX,T_{C^{-1}\cdot F(x)}\operatorname{Gr}(a,n)\bigr)$. The locus of maps from a $d$-dimensional space to a
$t$-dimensional space that are not surjective has codimension
$d-t+1$.\\

Consequently, the critical incidence locus
$\mathcal Z\subseteq\Omega$ satisfies
\[
   \dim\mathcal Z
   \le\dim\mathcal P_D+d-(d-t+1)
   =\dim\mathcal P_D+t-1.
\]
The generic fiber-dimension theorem, applied to the finitely
many irreducible components of $\mathcal Z$, gives a
nonempty open subset $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal P_D$
over which all fibers have dimension at most $t-1$.
Since $K$ is infinite, choose $H\in\mathcal U(K)$.
Finally, $V(0)=I_n$, so $\det V$ is a unit in $S_0$.
head: environment

label: thm:one-sided-complete
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Finite codimension of the tangent image is sufficient for finite determinacy
over an arbitrary field by the Greuel--Pham finite-determinacy criterion
\cite[Theorem~3.1.12]{GLS}.  Over a finite field, the assertion in the
dimension ranges stated above is precisely
Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-ranges}, together with the equivalence between
ordinary and extended tangent-image codimension.  It therefore remains to
prove necessity when $K$ is infinite. In characteristic zero, necessity follows from separability of the finite-jet
orbit maps; see \cite[Theorem~3.1.21]{GLS} and
\cite[Theorem~4.3]{GP18}. We may therefore assume that $\operatorname{char} K=p>0$. We prove the assertion for $\mathcal G_l$.  The $\mathcal G_r$ case follows by transposition.\\

Assume that $A$ is finitely $\mathcal G_l$-determined, and let $k$ be a determinacy
order.  Replacing $A$ by a polynomial truncation in its $\mathcal G_l$-orbit, we may
suppose that the entries of $A$ belong to $S_0$.  We use the same symbol $A$
for this algebraic representative and for its completion. Finite $\mathcal G_l$-determinacy implies finite $\mathcal G_{lr}$-determinacy.  Therefore
Theorem~\ref{thm:glr}, together with
Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-trans}, shows that $A$ is transverse to every
constant-rank stratum on the punctured formal spectrum.\\ 

Fix a rank $r$.  If the rank-$r$ locus has no punctured point, there is
nothing to prove.  We therefore assume that it does.  Put $c=(m-r)(n-r)$ and $d=s-c$.  By Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new}, the rank-at-most-$r$ locus has the
expected codimension $c$, and its punctured rank-$r$ stratum is smooth of
pure dimension $d$. Let $F=\kappa_r\circ A$ be the kernel map on the rank-$r$ stratum, and put $t=\dim\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)=r(n-r)$. If $t=0$, the Grassmannian is a point, and therefore there is no kernel-map
obstruction.  Thus assume that $t>0$.\\

We carry out all incidence and image-dimension arguments on
algebraic representatives in an open neighborhood
$U\subseteq\mathbb A_K^s$ of the origin, before localizing.
After shrinking $U$, the punctured rank-$r$ locus is smooth
of pure dimension $d=s-(m-r)(n-r)$.  When passing to the local ring and its completion, we use
the reduced closures of the relevant locally closed loci.
Their completed germs are identified by the formal source
automorphisms arising from finite determinacy. Completion
preserves the dimension of these closed local germs.
Components of an algebraic closure that do not contain the
origin are removed by shrinking $U$.
Thus the resulting dimension bounds also bound the
algebraic image closures used below.\\

We first show that $t\le d$. 
Let $X_{r,1},\ldots,X_{r,a}$ be the finitely many algebraic irreducible components of the punctured
rank-$r$ locus, and let $Y_j=\overline{F(X_{r,j})}
\subseteq\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)$ 
be their image closures.  Since $\dim X_{r,j}=d$, 
we have that $\dim Y_j\le d$ for every $j$. Choose a generic prime $\mathfrak q$ of a formal irreducible component of
the completed rank-$r$ locus, and put $L=\operatorname{Frac}\left(\frac{R}{\mathfrak q}\right)$. \\

Let $V$ be a sufficiently deep polynomial gauge with $dV=0$.
Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-gauge-rigidity} gives a formal source automorphism
$\varphi_V$ preserving every determinantal rank locus such that, on the
completed rank-$r$ locus we have that $V^{-1}\!\cdot F=F\circ\varphi_V$. 
The automorphism $\varphi_V$ permutes the finitely many formal irreducible
components.  Every such formal component lies over one of the algebraic
components $X_{r,j}$.  Therefore $V(\mathfrak q)^{-1}\!\cdot F(\mathfrak q)
\in
\bigcup_{j=1}^a (Y_j)_L$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:frobenius-gauge-flexibility}, the possible values
$V(\mathfrak q)$ are Zariski dense in $\operatorname{GL}_n(L)$.  Since $\operatorname{GL}_n$ acts
transitively on $\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)$, the corresponding points $V(\mathfrak q)^{-1}\!\cdot F(\mathfrak q)$
are Zariski dense in the Grassmannian after base change to $L$.
Consequently
\[
\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)_L
\subseteq
\bigcup_{j=1}^a(Y_j)_L.
\]
The Grassmannian is irreducible.  Hence one of the $Y_j$ is the whole
Grassmannian.  Therefore $t\le d$, 
as claimed.\\

We may now apply
Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-gauge-general-position} to the punctured algebraic
rank-$r$ locus.  Taking the depth at least $k$, we obtain some $V\in\operatorname{GL}_n(S_0)$ such that $
V-I_n\in\mathfrak m_0^kM_n(S_0)$ and $\dim\operatorname{Crit}(V^{-1}\!\cdot F)\le t-1$. Since $A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}$, we have that $AV-A\in\mathfrak m^{k+1}M_{m,n}$. 
Finite $\mathcal G_l$-$k$-determinacy therefore gives $AV\sim_{\mathcal G_l}A$.  By Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-gauge-rigidity}, the corresponding completed kernel
maps differ by a formal source automorphism.  The chain rule therefore
identifies their completed critical schemes.  Completion preserves the
dimension of the corresponding local schemes, and hence the critical locus
of the original completed kernel map also satisfies $\dim\operatorname{Crit}(F)\le t-1$. \\

We claim that this critical locus is in fact empty on the punctured spectrum.
Suppose otherwise.  Let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_b$
be the algebraic irreducible components of the critical locus of $F$ on the
punctured rank-$r$ stratum.  The preceding bound gives $\dim Z_i\le t-1$ for every $i$.  Put $W_i=\overline{F(Z_i)}
\subseteq\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)$.
Thus $\dim W_i\le t-1$. \\

Choose a generic prime $\mathfrak q$ of a formal irreducible component of
the completed critical locus.  Let $V$ now range over sufficiently deep
polynomial gauges satisfying $dV=0$. 
Therefore, the differential of $V^{-1}\!\cdot F$ is obtained from $dF$
by composition with an invertible linear map on the target tangent space.
Therefore the critical scheme of $V^{-1}\!\cdot F$ is exactly the critical
scheme of $F$.

On the other hand, Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-gauge-rigidity} gives $V^{-1}\!\cdot F=F\circ\varphi_V$. 
Thus $\varphi_V$ preserves the completed critical locus and permutes its
finitely many formal irreducible components.  Therefore, for $L=\operatorname{Frac}\left(\frac{R}{\mathfrak q}\right)$,  we get that 
\[
V(\mathfrak q)^{-1}\!\cdot F(\mathfrak q)
\in
\bigcup_{i=1}^b(W_i)_L.
\]

Lemma~\ref{lem:frobenius-gauge-flexibility} again shows that the values
$V(\mathfrak q)$ are Zariski dense in $\operatorname{GL}_n(L)$.  Hence the left-hand side
is Zariski dense in $\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)_L$.  We would therefore obtain $\operatorname{Gr}(n-r,n)_L
\subseteq
\bigcup_{i=1}^b(W_i)_L$.
This is impossible since the left-hand side is irreducible of dimension
$t$, whereas every $W_i$ has dimension at most $t-1$.  Thus we can conclude that $\operatorname{Crit}(F)=\varnothing$
on the punctured rank-$r$ locus. Therefore, we can conclude that every kernel map of the form  $\kappa_r\circ A$ is submersive on the corresponding punctured constant-rank stratum.
Proposition~\ref{prop:one-sided-criterion} therefore implies that the
extended $\mathcal G_l$ tangent image has finite $K$-codimension. Finally, the ordinary tangent image differs from the extended tangent image
only by replacing the $R$-span of the finitely many derivative matrices by
their $\mathfrak m$-span.  The quotient between these two derivative contributions is
finite-dimensional over $K$.  Thus finite codimension of the ordinary and
extended tangent images are equivalent.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Over an infinite field,
Theorem~\ref{thm:glr}, Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-right}, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-complete} give necessity and sufficiency of the
tangent-image criterion for all four actions, namely $\mathcal R, \mathcal G_l, \mathcal G_r,\mathcal G_{lr}$. 
Over a finite field, the full left--right and pure right criteria remain
valid over arbitrary fields, while the one-sided equivalence is established
in the dimension ranges of Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-ranges}.  The
unrestricted finite-field one-sided case would require an additional
finite-field general-position theorem replacing
Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-gauge-general-position}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Finite codimension of the tangent image can be checked by the
standard-basis methods developed by Greuel--Pham
\cite{GreuelPham2020}.  Consequently, over an infinite field the preceding
theorems give a decision criterion for finite determinacy for all four
matrix actions whenever the ground field is given in an effective form.
Over finite fields, the same conclusion holds for the full left--right and
pure right actions and, for the one-sided actions, in the ranges of
Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-ranges}.

label: lem:deep-shear-new
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:deep-shear-new}
Let $T=K[[y_1,\ldots,y_q]]$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_T$.  Suppose a proper ideal
$D\subseteq T$ is invariant under every sufficiently deep triangular automorphism and
contains a nonzero polynomial.  Then $\sqrt D=\mathfrak m_T$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $0\ne P\in D\cap K[y_1,\ldots,y_q]$.  Fix $j$.  For $i\ne j$ choose
integers $M_i$ larger than the depth from which triangular automorphisms preserve $D$
and, successively, so large that the map
$\alpha\longmapsto
  \alpha_j+\sum_{i\ne j}M_i\alpha_i.$
is injective on the finite support of $P$.  Apply the triangular automorphism
$\sigma_j$ given by $y_i\mapsto y_i+y_j^{M_i}$ for $i\ne j$ and
$y_j\mapsto y_j$.  In $\sigma_j(P)$, select from each substituted factor the
pure $y_j$-term.  Injectivity of the displayed weight on the support implies that
one original monomial contributes a unique largest pure power of $y_j$, with
nonzero coefficient.  Fix once and for all a degree-compatible monomial order on
$K[y_1,\ldots,y_q]$.  Because every $M_i>1$, within the expansion of any fixed
monomial of $P$ the term obtained by choosing the pure $y_j^{M_i}$ contribution from
each substituted factor has strictly largest total degree.  Choosing the $M_i$
successively and sufficiently large makes these maximal total degrees distinct for the
finitely many monomials in the support of $P$.  Thus $\sigma_j(P)$ has a unique
highest-total-degree term, and that term is a positive power of $y_j$; in particular it
is the leading monomial for the fixed degree-compatible order.\\

Put $J=D\cap K[y_1,\ldots,y_q]$. The initial ideal of $J$
contains a power of every variable, so $K[y]/J$ is
zero-dimensional. Since $J\subseteq\langle y\rangle$,
its localization at $\langle y\rangle$ is a proper
zero-dimensional local ring. Therefore, for some $b$, we have that $\langle y\rangle^bK[y]_{\langle y\rangle}
  \subseteq JK[y]_{\langle y\rangle}$. Extending to $K[[y]]$ gives
$\mathfrak m_T^b\subseteq D$, and therefore
$\sqrt D=\mathfrak m_T$.
head: environment

label: lem:critical-height-new
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:critical-height-new}
Assume $2\le q\le s$ and let $F\in\mathfrak m K[x]^q$ satisfy
$\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)(0)\bigr)<q$.  For every $N$ there is $H\in\mathfrak m^N K[x]^q$ such
that, for $G=F+H$, the ideal $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ has height $s-q+1$ after localization
and completion at the origin.  Moreover the \emph{critical-value ideal}
\[
 \Delta_G=\ker\!\left(
 K[[y_1,\ldots,y_q]]\longrightarrow \frac{R}{I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))},
 \quad y_i\longmapsto G_i
 \right)
\]
contains a nonzero polynomial.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First replace $N$ by a larger integer if necessary.  Choose pairwise distinct integers
$a_1,\ldots,a_q\ge N$, none divisible by $\operatorname{char} K$, and larger than the
degrees occurring in $F$, and set
$H_i=\sum_{j=1}^s x_j^{a_i}$.
For a $q$-element subset $J=\{j_1,\ldots,j_q\}$ of the source variables, the part of
highest total degree in the corresponding $q\times q$ Jacobian minor is
$\det\bigl[a_i x_{j_\ell}^{a_i-1}\bigr]_{1\le i,\ell\le q}$.
This generalized alternant is nonzero: after expansion, distinct permutations give
distinct exponent vectors because the $a_i$ are distinct, and every coefficient
$\prod_i a_i$ is nonzero in $K$. Choose a degree-compatible monomial order. For every
$q$-element subset $J$, the leading monomial of the
corresponding Jacobian minor is therefore a monomial of
the highest-total-degree alternant. Its support is exactly
$J$, and each variable indexed by $J$ has positive exponent.  Its leading monomial has a strictly positive exponent on every
variable indexed by $J$ and no other variables.  Therefore a positive power of
$\prod_{j\in J}x_j$ belongs to the initial ideal.  Hence the radical of the initial ideal
of $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ contains the squarefree monomial ideal generated by
$\prod_{j\in J}x_j$ over all $q$-element subsets $J$.  That squarefree ideal has height
$s-q+1$.  A Gr\"obner degeneration preserves Krull dimension \cite[Chapter~15]{Eisenbud1995}, so
$\operatorname{ht} I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))=\operatorname{ht}\operatorname{in}(I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G)))\ge s-q+1$; the standard determinantal height bound \cite[Chapter~2]{BrunsVetter} gives the reverse inequality.  Thus equality holds in
$K[x_1,\ldots,x_s]$.  Since $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(G)(0)\bigr)<q$, every maximal minor vanishes at the
origin, so $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))\subseteq \langle x_1,\ldots,x_s\rangle$.  Every prime contained in this maximal
ideal and minimal over $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ has height at least $s-q+1$, while the determinantal
height bound remains valid after localization.  Hence the localized ideal has height
exactly $s-q+1$.  Completion preserves the dimension of the quotient
\cite[Lemma~15.44.1, Tag~07NV]{stacks-project}, and therefore preserves the height in
this regular local ring.  This proves the stated local and completed assertion.\\

Every minimal component of the critical locus consequently has dimension at most
$q-1$.  The restrictions of the $q$ functions $G_1,\ldots,G_q$ to such a component
are algebraically dependent, so for each minimal component there is a nonzero
polynomial $P(y_1,\ldots,y_q)$ vanishing on its image.  Multiplying these relations over
the finitely many minimal components gives a nonzero polynomial in the radical of the
kernel of
$K[y_1,\ldots,y_q]\longrightarrow \frac{K[x_1,\ldots,x_s]}{I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))}, \qquad y_i\longmapsto G_i$.
Taking a suitable power produces a nonzero polynomial in the kernel itself.  This is the
asserted critical-value relation.

label: thm:pure-right
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:pure-right}
For every field $K$ and every $F\in\mathfrak m R^q$,
\[
 F\text{ is finitely }\mathcal R\text{-determined}
 \iff \dim_K \left(\frac{R^q}{\operatorname{ima}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)\bigr)}\right)<\infty.
\]
If $q>1$, these conditions are equivalent to $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)(0)\bigr)=q$.  In that case
$q\le s$, the germ $F$ is right equivalent to the coordinate projection
$(x_1,\ldots,x_q)$, and $F$ is already $1$-$\mathcal R$-determined.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $q=1$, the assertion is the arbitrary-characteristic finite-Milnor-number
criterion \cite[Theorem~2.1]{BoubakriGreuelMarkwig2012}.  Assume $q>1$.  Proposition~\ref{prop:dimension-bounds} gives $q\le s$.
After replacing $F$ by a polynomial truncation in its right orbit, define its
\emph{relation ideal} and \emph{critical-value ideal} by
$E_F=\ker(K[[y_1,\ldots,y_q]]\to R,\ y_i\mapsto F_i)$ and
$\Delta_F=\ker(K[[y_1,\ldots,y_q]]\to \frac{R}{I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(F))},\ y_i\mapsto F_i)$,
respectively.  Let $k$ be a right-determinacy order for $F$.  If a target automorphism $\psi$ satisfies
$\psi(y)-y\in\mathfrak m_T^{k+1}T^q$, then $F_i\in\mathfrak m$ gives
$\psi\circ F-F\in\mathfrak m^{k+1}R^q$.  Hence $\psi\circ F$ is right equivalent to $F$, so
there is a source automorphism $\varphi$ with $\psi\circ F=F\circ\varphi$.  For such
$\psi$, the chain rule gives
$\operatorname{JacMat}(\psi\circ F)=D\psi(F)\operatorname{JacMat}(F)$ with $D\psi(F)$ invertible.  Thus the maximal-minor
ideal is unchanged up to the induced source automorphism, and both $E_F$ and
$\Delta_F$ are invariant under these deep target automorphisms.\\

We first record the following consequence of right determinacy, which we use in the
proof: the
components of $F$ minimally generate the ideal $\langle F_1,\ldots,F_q\rangle$.  Indeed, suppose
after reordering that $F_q\in I_0=\langle F_1,\ldots,F_{q-1}\rangle$.  Since $q\le s$, the ideal
$I_0$ has at most $s-1$ generators and therefore is not $\mathfrak m$-primary.  Thus, for every
$N$, one can choose $h\in\mathfrak m^N\setminus I_0$.  Take $N$ larger than a right-determinacy
order and set $G=(F_1,\ldots,F_{q-1},F_q+h)$.  Then $G=\varphi(F)$ for some source
automorphism $\varphi$.  For $i<q$ this identity gives $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, whereas
applying $\varphi$ to a relation $F_q=\sum_{i<q}a_iF_i$ gives
$F_q+h=\sum_{i<q}\varphi(a_i)F_i$, so $h\in I_0$, a contradiction.\\

Suppose $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)(0)\bigr)<q$.  Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:critical-height-new} beyond the
determinacy order.  The resulting right-equivalent $G$ has a critical-value ideal
containing a nonzero polynomial, so Lemma~\ref{lem:deep-shear-new} gives
$\sqrt{\Delta_G}=\mathfrak m_T$.  Thus every component $G_i$ belongs to the radical of
$I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$.\\

Right determinacy implies finite contact determinacy of the generator column.  If
$q<s$, Corollary~\ref{cor:icis-all-fields} shows that
$\langle G_1,\ldots,G_q\rangle$ defines an ICIS.  Therefore
$\langle G_1,\ldots,G_q\rangle+I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary.  Since every $G_i$ lies in
$\sqrt{I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))}$, these two ideals have the same radical, and $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ would itself
be $\mathfrak m$-primary.  If $q=s$ and $\langle G_1,\ldots,G_q\rangle$ were not $\mathfrak m$-primary, then it would
have positive-dimensional quotient; Corollary~\ref{cor:icis-all-fields} would make its
$q=s$ minimal generators a regular sequence, forcing a zero-dimensional quotient, a
contradiction.  Thus $\langle G_1,\ldots,G_q\rangle$ is $\mathfrak m$-primary.  The same radical
containment therefore forces
$I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(G))$ to be $\mathfrak m$-primary.  Both alternatives are impossible because a proper
maximal-minor ideal of a $q\times s$ matrix has height at most $s-q+1<s$.  Hence
$\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)(0)\bigr)=q$.\\

A full-rank Jacobian at the origin makes $F$ a formal submersion, so a source coordinate
change sends it to $(x_1,\ldots,x_q)$.  Any germ with the same $1$-jet as $F$ again has
Jacobian rank $q$ at the origin and is therefore right equivalent to the same coordinate
projection.  Hence $F$ is $1$-$\mathcal R$-determined.  Conversely, if
$\frac{R^q}{\operatorname{ima}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(F)\bigr)}$ has finite length, then the Jacobian map is surjective after
localization at every nonmaximal prime.  Thus no nonmaximal prime contains the ideal
$I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(F))$ of maximal minors, and hence $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(F))$ is either $\mathfrak m$-primary or the unit
ideal.  Tensoring with $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ also shows that $\operatorname{JacMat}(F)$ has row rank $q$, so necessarily
$q\le s$.  The determinantal height bound \cite[Chapter~2]{BrunsVetter}
$\operatorname{ht} I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(F))\le s-q+1<s$ excludes the proper $\mathfrak m$-primary case when $q>1$,
so $I_q(\operatorname{JacMat}(F))=R$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The rigidity in Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-right} is specific to pure right equivalence.  When
$q>1$, a finitely right-determined map germ cannot have a singular differential at the origin:
it is already a formal submersion and hence a coordinate projection.  For example,
\[
 (x_1^2,x_2,\ldots,x_q):(K^s,0)\longrightarrow(K^q,0)
\]
is never finitely pure-right determined for $q>1$, in any characteristic.  This should be
contrasted with left--right and contact equivalence, where non-submersive finitely determined
germs are the principal objects of singularity theory.
head: environment

label: cor:smooth-target-right
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:smooth-target-right}
Let $(Y,y)$ be smooth with $y\in Y(K)$ and $\dim_yY=q>1$, and let
$F:(\operatorname{Spf} R,\mathfrak m)\to(\widehat Y_y,y)$ be a formal map germ.  Then $F$ is
finitely right determined if and only if $dF_0:T_0\mathbb A_K^s\to T_yY$ is surjective.  In
this case $F$ is $1$-right-determined.  These statements do not depend on the choice of
formal parameters at $y$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $Y$ is smooth at the $K$-rational point $y$, its completed local ring is
(noncanonically) isomorphic to $K[[y_1,\ldots,y_q]]$. Under such an
isomorphism the assertion is exactly Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-right}. Replacing
one regular system of parameters by another composes the coordinate
representative with a target formal automorphism; this preserves
surjectivity of $dF_0$ and the property that all germs with the same
$1$-jet lie in one source-coordinate orbit.
head: environment

label: cor:pure-right-matrix
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:pure-right-matrix}
Let $A\in\mathfrak m M_{m,n}$ over an arbitrary field.  Then $A$ is finitely
$\mathcal R$-determined if and only if its ordinary, equivalently its extended,
$\mathcal R$-tangent image has finite $K$-codimension.  If $mn>1$, these
conditions are equivalent to surjectivity at the origin of the
differential of the entry map $A:(K^s,0)\longrightarrow(K^{mn},0)$, 
and in this case $A$ is already $1$-$\mathcal R$-determined. Consequently, Theorems~\ref{thm:glr} and~\ref{thm:pure-right} settle the
full left--right and pure right cases of GLS Conjecture~3.1.16 over every
field.  Together with Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-complete}, they settle
all four actions over every infinite field.  Over an arbitrary field,
the one-sided cases are additionally settled in the dimension ranges of
Theorem~\ref{thm:one-sided-ranges}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Vectorize the entries of $A$ and apply
Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-right} with $q=mn$.  The extended $\mathcal R$-tangent
image is the $R$-span of the derivative matrices, whereas the ordinary
$\mathcal R$-tangent image is their $\mathfrak m$-span.  The quotient of the former
derivative contribution by the latter is generated over $K$ by the
finitely many derivative matrices.  Therefore finite codimension of the
ordinary tangent image is equivalent to finite codimension of the
extended tangent image.

If $mn>1$, Theorem~\ref{thm:pure-right} shows that finite right
determinacy is equivalent to having $\operatorname{rank}\bigl(\operatorname{JacMat}(A)(0)\bigr)=mn$.  This is exactly surjectivity at the origin of the differential of the
entry map $A:(K^s,0)\longrightarrow(K^{mn},0)$. 
The same theorem then shows that $A$ is $1$-$\mathcal R$-determined.  For
$mn=1$, the assertion is the scalar finite-right-determinacy criterion.
head: environment

label: cor:rank-trans
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rank}, punctured transversality is equivalent to localized
surjectivity of the extended left--right tangent image.  For a finitely generated
cokernel over $R$, this is equivalent to finite length.  Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:glr}.
head: environment

label: thm:det-geometry-new
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:det-geometry-new}
Let $G\in\{\mathcal R,\mathcal G_l,\mathcal G_r,\mathcal G_{lr}\}$ and let $A$ be finitely $G$-determined.  Then
\[
 \operatorname{ht} I_t(A)=\min\{s,c_t\}\qquad(1\le t\le\min(m,n)).
\]
Moreover $\frac{R}{I_t(A)}$ is Cohen--Macaulay; if $c_t<s$ it is reduced; and if
$c_t\le s-2$ it is a normal domain.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Finite $G$-determinacy implies finite $\mathcal G_{lr}$-determinacy.  At every nonmaximal point
lying over $I_t(A)$, Corollary~\ref{cor:rank-trans} gives the expected inverse-image
codimension.  Combined with the standard determinantal height bound \cite[Chapter~2]{BrunsVetter}, this proves the
height formula.  If $c_t\le s$, the equality $\operatorname{ht} I_t(A)=c_t$ is the
expected-height case, so determinantal perfection gives Cohen--Macaulayness
\cite[Chapter~2]{BrunsVetter}.  If $c_t>s$, then $\operatorname{ht} I_t(A)=s$ and
$\frac{R}{I_t(A)}$ is zero-dimensional, hence Cohen--Macaulay.\\

If $c_t<s$, every minimal prime lies in the punctured spectrum and has generic matrix
rank $t-1$.  Transversality makes the quotient smooth at every generic point.  It is therefore generically reduced.  Since a Cohen--Macaulay ring has no embedded associated primes \cite[Lemma~10.103.7, Tag~0BUS]{stacks-project}, it is reduced.\\

Assume $c_t\le s-2$.  Then
\[
 \dim\left(\frac{R}{I_t(A)}\right)=s-c_t\ge2,
\]
so the closed point has codimension at least two in the determinantal quotient and is irrelevant
for Serre condition $R_1$.  On the punctured spectrum, transversality identifies the singular
locus with the inverse image of the matrices of rank at most $t-2$.  If $t=1$ this locus is empty.
If $t\ge2$, its codimension in $\frac{R}{I_t(A)}$ is at least $ \min\{s,c_{t-1}\}-c_t\ge2$. Thus every codimension-one point is regular, so $R_1$ holds.  Cohen--Macaulayness gives $S_2$,
and the Serre criterion \cite[Lemma~10.157.4, Tag~031S]{stacks-project} gives normality.  Since
the quotient is local, a normal ring is a domain.
head: environment

label: cor:det-approx-new
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:det-approx-new}
Every prescribed finite matrix jet over any field admits a higher-order completion for
which all determinantal ideals simultaneously have the heights and regularity properties
of Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new}.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:jettrans}.  The resulting matrix
has finite left--right tangent-image codimension and is therefore finitely
$\mathcal G_{lr}$-determined.  Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:det-geometry-new}.

label: def:rosenlicht-modality
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:rosenlicht-modality}
Let an algebraic group $G$ act on a variety $X$.  A \emph{Rosenlicht
stratification} is a finite disjoint decomposition $X=\coprod_aX_a$ into
$G$-invariant locally closed subvarieties for which geometric quotient morphisms
$\pi_a:X_a\to Q_a$ exist.  Here a \emph{geometric quotient} means a surjective
$G$-invariant morphism whose geometric fibers are precisely the $G$-orbits and whose
regular functions are the invariant regular functions; the symbol $Q_a$ denotes the
corresponding quotient variety.  Such stratifications exist by
Rosenlicht \cite{Rosenlicht1956,Rosenlicht1963}.  For an open neighborhood $U$ of $x\in X$, set
$G\text{-mod}(U)=\max_a\dim\pi_a(U\cap X_a)$ and define $G\text{-mod}(x)$ as the
minimum of this number over all open neighborhoods $U$ of $x$.  The result is
independent of the chosen Rosenlicht stratification
\cite[Definition~2.1 and Corollary~A.3]{GreuelNguyen2016}.  Thus
$G\text{-mod}(x)$ measures the local dimension of the orbit space near $x$---the
number of essential parameters left after quotienting by $G$---rather than the
dimension of the orbit itself.\\

For an isolated hypersurface germ $f$, an integer $N$ is \emph{sufficiently large for
right equivalence} if some neighborhood of $j^Nf$ in $\mathcal J_N$ consists entirely of right
$N$-determined germs.  The \emph{right modality} is
$\operatorname{Rmod}(f)=\mathcal R_N\text{-mod}(j^Nf)$ for any such $N$; it is independent of the choice
of sufficiently large $N$ \cite[Definitions~2.1, 2.3 and Proposition~2.4]{GreuelNguyen2016}.
head: environment

label: def:proper-modality
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:proper-modality}
Let $(T,t_0)$ be a pointed algebraic variety.  An \emph{unfolding with trivial section}
of $f$ over $(T,t_0)$ is a family $F(x,t)\in\mathcal O(T)[[x]]$ such that
$F(x,t_0)=f$ and $F(0,t)=0$ for every $t$.  It is \emph{right-complete} if every
unfolding of $f$ becomes, after passage to an étale neighborhood of its base point,
fiberwise right equivalent to a pullback of $F$; see
\cite[Definition~2.9]{GreuelNguyen2016}.  A semiuniversal unfolding with trivial
section has the form
$F(x,t)=f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^{b_f}t_jg_j(x)$, where the classes of the $g_j$ form a
$k$-basis of $\frac{\mathfrak m}{\mathfrak m\operatorname{Jac}(f)}$ and $b_f=\mu(f)+n-1$; it is right-complete
\cite[Proposition~2.14]{GreuelNguyen2016}.\\

For any unfolding $F$, the notation $\mathcal R\text{-mod}_F(f)$ denotes the local
number of parameters that remain after quotienting the image of the parameter-to-jet map
$t\mapsto j^NF_t$ by the $\mathcal R_N$-action, computed on a Rosenlicht stratification; more
precisely it is the relative Rosenlicht modality at $t_0$ for a sufficiently large
$N$.  It is independent of that choice \cite[Definition~2.5]{GreuelNguyen2016}.  For a semiuniversal unfolding
with trivial section, let
$\mathcal C_{\mu(f)}(F)=\{t\mid\mu(F_t)=\mu(f)\}$ be its Milnor-constant stratum.
Following Nguyen, the \emph{proper modality} is
$\operatorname{pmod}(f)=\dim_{t_0}\mathcal C_{\mu(f)}(F)$ \cite[\S2.2]{Nguyen2019}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The notion of modality was introduced into singularity theory in the classification of
simple, unimodal, and bimodal singularities by Arnold and collaborators; see \cite{AGV}.
The algebraic formulation used here replaces a local analytic orbit space by Rosenlicht
quotients and was developed in arbitrary characteristic by Greuel--Nguyen
\cite{GreuelNguyen2016}.  In the complex analytic setting, Gabrielov proved that modality
agrees with proper modality \cite{Gabrielov1974}.  Nguyen established the corresponding
positive-characteristic equality first for univariate germs and later for all right
unimodal and bimodal germs \cite{Nguyen2014,Nguyen2019}.
head: environment

label: lem:standard-inputs
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:standard-inputs}
Let $f\in\mathfrak m^2\subseteq R=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ be isolated.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*]
\item\label{std:suff} Every $N\ge 2\mu(f)$ is sufficiently large for right equivalence in the
sense of Definition~\ref{def:rosenlicht-modality}.
\item\label{std:complete} For every unfolding $F$ of $f$ one has
$\mathcal R\text{-mod}_F(f)\le\operatorname{Rmod}(f)$; equality holds for a right-complete unfolding.  In
particular, a semiuniversal unfolding with trivial section is right-complete.
\item\label{std:sep} For an algebraic finite-jet action, the orbit map is separable if and only
if its differential at the identity is surjective onto the tangent space of the orbit; equivalently,
the tangent image equals the orbit tangent space.
\item\label{std:group} Over a perfect field, the reduction of a finite-type group scheme is a
closed subgroup scheme, and every reduced finite-type group scheme is smooth.
\item\label{std:det}  If
$\mathfrak m^{N+2}\subseteq\mathfrak m^2\operatorname{Jac}(f)$, then $f$ is right
$(2N-\operatorname{ord}(f)+2)$-determined.
\item\label{std:MY} Put
\[
 M_N(f)=\frac{R}{\mathfrak m^N\operatorname{Jac}(f)},
\]
and regard it as a $k[[t]]$-algebra via $t\mapsto f$.  If $s=\operatorname{ord}(f)$ and
$d(f)=\operatorname{ord}(\operatorname{Jac}(f))$, then for every $N$ satisfying
\[
 \mathfrak m^{\left\lfloor\frac{N+s+d(f)+1}{2}\right\rfloor}\subseteq\mathfrak m^2\operatorname{Jac}(f)
\]
one has
\[
 f\overset{\mathcal R}{\sim}g
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 M_N(f)\cong M_N(g)\quad\text{as $k[[t]]$-algebras}.
\]
\item\label{std:split}
There is a right equivalence $f\overset{\mathcal R}{\sim}
g(x_1,\ldots,x_c)+Q(x_{c+1},\ldots,x_{n})$, 
where $Q$ is a nonsingular quadratic form in the split variables, with the zero-variable case allowed, and $\operatorname{Hess}(g)(0)=0$. If $p\ne2$, then $g\in\langle x_1,\ldots,x_c\rangle^3$; if $p=2$, the quadratic part of $g$ is the square of a linear form. The residual germ is unique up to right equivalence. In particular, $c$ is invariant under right equivalence, and right modality is invariant under nonsingular quadratic suspension.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: Standard inputs for right equivalence

title: Proof
body_md:
For Assertion~\ref{std:suff}, choose a jet order large enough that the Jacobian colength is
computed in the corresponding truncated power-series ring.  On that finite-dimensional jet
space, $\mu$ is the dimension of the cokernel of a matrix whose entries depend algebraically
on the jet coefficients, and is therefore upper semicontinuous.  Hence, after shrinking around
$j^Nf$, every nearby germ $g$ has $\mu(g)\le\mu(f)$.  Boubakri--Greuel--Markwig
\cite[Theorem~2.1(a) and Corollary~2.4(a)]{BoubakriGreuelMarkwig2012} show that an
isolated $g$ is right determined of order at most
$2\mu(g)-\operatorname{ord}(g)+2\le2\mu(g)$.  Thus every $N\ge2\mu(f)$ is sufficiently large in
the sense of Definition~\ref{def:rosenlicht-modality}.  The independence of right modality
from the choice of a sufficiently large jet is \cite[Proposition~2.4]{GreuelNguyen2016}.
Assertion~\ref{std:complete} is \cite[Proposition~2.12(ii) and
Proposition~2.14]{GreuelNguyen2016}.  Assertion~\ref{std:sep} is the standard separability
criterion for algebraic group orbits; see \cite[Corollary~4.2]{GreuelPham2020} and
\cite[Proposition~3.1.17]{GLS}.  Assertion~\ref{std:group} is
\cite[Lemmas~39.7.6 and~39.8.4, Tags~047R and~047P]{stacks-project}.
Assertion~\ref{std:det} is \cite[Theorem~2.1(a)]{BoubakriGreuelMarkwig2012}, and
Assertion~\ref{std:MY} is \cite[Theorem~2.4]{GreuelPhamMY2017}.  Finally,
Assertion~\ref{std:split} is the existence-and-uniqueness form of the splitting
lemma of Greuel--Pfister \cite{GreuelPfister2026}; the invariance of right modality
under nonsingular quadratic suspension follows from
\cite[\S3]{GreuelNguyen2016}.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Over the complex numbers, the Mather--Yau theorem determines an isolated hypersurface
singularity from its moduli algebra \cite{MatherYau1982}.  The literal analogue fails in
positive characteristic; the higher Milnor-algebra form used in
Lemma~\ref{lem:standard-inputs}\ref{std:MY} is the replacement proved by
Greuel--Pham \cite{GreuelPhamMY2017}.  The splitting lemma is classical in
characteristic different from two; the form used here, including characteristic two,
is due to Greuel--Pfister \cite{GreuelPfister2026}.

label: lem:regular
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:regular}
If $f$ is isolated, then $\partial_1f,\ldots,\partial_nf$ is a regular sequence.  Every
syzygy $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)\in R^n$ satisfying $\sum_i z_i\partial_i f=0$ is generated
by Koszul syzygies; in particular every $z_i$ belongs to $\operatorname{Jac}(f)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal $\operatorname{Jac}(f)$ has height $n$ and is generated by $n$ elements.
The regular local ring $R$ is Cohen--Macaulay of dimension $n$
\cite[Lemma~10.106.3, Tag~00NQ]{stacks-project}.  Hence these generators form a system
of parameters and therefore a regular sequence
\cite[Lemma~10.104.2, Tag~02JN]{stacks-project}.  Exactness of the Koszul complex
\cite[Lemma~15.31.2, Tag~062F]{stacks-project} gives the syzygy assertion, and every
coordinate of a Koszul syzygy lies in $\operatorname{Jac}(f)$.
head: environment

label: lem:taylor
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to consider a monomial $x^\alpha$.  The multivariable binomial
formula gives
\[
 (x+Y)^\alpha
 =x^\alpha+\sum_i\alpha_i x^{\alpha-e_i}Y_i
 +\sum_{\substack{\beta\le\alpha\\|\beta|\ge2}}
 \binom{\alpha}{\beta}x^{\alpha-\beta}Y^\beta.
\]
The middle sum is
$\sum_i\left(\frac{\partial x^\alpha}{\partial x_i}\right)Y_i$, while every term in the last
sum lies in $\langle Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\rangle^2$.  Applying this termwise to
$f=\sum_\alpha c_\alpha x^\alpha$ is legitimate in the $\langle x_1,\ldots,x_n,Y_1,\ldots,Y_n\rangle$-adic
topology.  No division by factorials occurs.
head: environment

label: lem:integrate
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma~\ref{lem:regular}, $z_i\in \operatorname{Jac}(f)\subseteq\mathfrak m$.  Seek
$\Phi_t(x_i)=x_i+U_i(t,x),\qquad U_i=tz_i+\sum_{r\ge2}t^ru_i^{(r)},\qquad u_i^{(r)}\in \operatorname{Jac}(f)$.
Assume the coefficients below order $r$ have been chosen so that
$f(x+U)-f(x)\equiv0\pmod{t^r}$, and let $E_r$ be the coefficient of $t^r$
before $u^{(r)}$ is chosen.  In \eqref{eq:taylor}, every nonlinear term has
at least two $U$-factors, hence lies in $\operatorname{Jac}(f)^2$.  The already chosen linear
part has no new $t^r$ term.  Thus
$E_r\in \operatorname{Jac}(f)^2=\sum_i(\partial_i f)\operatorname{Jac}(f)$, so choose $u_i^{(r)}\in \operatorname{Jac}(f)$ with
$\sum_i(\partial_i f)u_i^{(r)}=-E_r$.  The $t$-adic recursion produces
$U\in t\,\operatorname{Jac}(f)[[t]]^n$ with $f(x+U)=f(x)$.  Its linear coefficient matrix in the
$x$-variables is congruent to the identity modulo $t$, so the formal inverse-function theorem gives the required automorphism.
head: environment

label: def:eta
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:eta}
For isolated $f$, set
$\eta(f)=\min\{e\ge1\mid\mathfrak m^e\subseteq\mathfrak m\operatorname{Jac}(f)\}$.
If $d=\operatorname{ord}(f)$, then $\eta(f)\ge d$, because $\mathfrak m\operatorname{Jac}(f)\subseteq\mathfrak m^d$.
